**Wall-clock time** is real end-to-end elapsed time observed externally, from request or episode start to completion. It includes orchestration, queues, network delay, tool execution, retries, and provider inference.

**Provider inference time** is the interval spent by the model provider performing inference for a call. It is normally only one component of wall-clock time and excludes most client-side, network, queueing, and environment delays.

Conflating these clocks is scientifically invalid because they measure distinct causal and operational quantities. World time characterizes environmental dynamics; wall-clock time characterizes actual responsiveness and system latency; provider inference time characterizes model-service computation.
